notes: ENVIRONMENT: chromium.launch() times out after 180s on this machine (a wedged Metal compiler XPC service), so demo/validate/v5_packs.py could not be executed through Playwright. Every assertion in that file was executed instead as the equivalent DOM query against the running app in an already-open Chrome at http://127.0.0.1:8021, in a tab created for this evaluation, and the results are what this verdict records. Slices v2_filter, v3_critique, v4_themes and v4b_ingest recorded the same constraint the same way. Nothing in the script is machine-specific; re-run it once the host can launch a browser.

STALE BUNDLE RULED OUT before judging: the document loads /assets/index-B_gk10NF.js, a no-store refetch of it returns 427074 bytes with sha256 34f383453eaf24c53217474bd7215c7abf8b3a17e7650c54b6426ba1caa012ad, and that is byte-identical to frontend/dist/assets/index-B_gk10NF.js built at 19:34:49 — which postdates the 19:08:40 edit to PackPanel.tsx. So the DOM judged here is the current source, and no check rests on grepping the bundle for a marker string.

Quote resolution was asserted DOM against DOM. The pack's own quote_resolution field and the panel's 'quotes resolving 100%' chip were treated as claims to be tested, not evidence: for each of the 105 citations the chunk id was read off the link's title attribute, the video was opened in the RAG Pipeline corpus tree, and the quote was matched against the .chunkcard text the app renders for that chunk index. All 105 matched, in the cited chunk, with the link offset inside that chunk's rendered window. This is the check that would have caught the fabricated quote this project shipped once before, and it does not depend on any field the pack writes about itself.

The corpus moved under this evaluation. It read 59 videos / 1460 chunks in the V4b verdict, 60 / 1503 when the transcript sweep started, and 65 / 1654 an hour later with the header showing 'Indexing 1 · 0 queued'. Every count in this verdict is stated with the moment it was read. The pack's own figure (56 / 1372) did not move, which is the subject of the one failing check.

The one failing check is not a defect in what V5 built; it is a gap in what V5 says. Everything the slice brief asked to be established holds: four packs render with rubric counts matching their files, all 105 citations resolve to real transcript text at the right video and second, the multi-creator claim is honest down to the one rule that could have been inflated and was not, D2 is on screen as a three-way comparison with its noise ranges, no property video reaches any pack, and membership is both reviewable and genuinely overridable. What is missing is a sentence telling the reader that the pack in front of them was distilled from 56 of the corpus's now-65 videos.

D3's override is deliberately non-destructive by design and the panel says so ('overrides apply at the next build', 'nothing on screen changes until then'). That is a defensible choice — the rendered pack is the artifact on disk and only a rebuild can move it — but it does mean a reviewer cannot see the consequence of their own correction without leaving the app and running build-packs. Whether that is enough for 'overridable in the app' is a judgement; the mechanism is fully built and works end to end, so this verdict records it as passing.

THIS EVALUATION WROTE ONE FILE OUTSIDE ITS OWN ARTIFACT DIRECTORY: pressing the override control caused the server to rewrite experts/job-search/manifest.json. job-search was chosen because that directory is untracked, so no committed state changed. The overrides map was restored to {} by pressing 'auto'; the only residue is a new updated_at (2026-08-10T04:54:44 -> 2026-08-10T10:11:48) in an untracked file. Nothing else under experts/ was touched.

Routing quality is not scored here but a reader will notice it. system-design and app-architecture share two of their source units (raptor:theme:3 'Modular monoliths need vertical slicing and encapsulation' and community:27 'microservices, module, monolith…'), and three of the system-design pack's fifteen rules (r0101-r0103) are about module boundaries and encapsulation rather than distributed systems. Its membership table likewise routes in 'Exploring MLOps and LLMOps' (Databricks, 0.411) and 'Large Language Model Operations (LLMOps) Explained' (IBM Technology, 0.338). The rules are all distinct and all cited, so nothing here is fabricated — but 'system design' as this pack defines it is looser than the routing text describes, and the two lowest-scoring members of each pack are the place to look first if a reviewer wants to tighten it.

The gap lists are the strongest evidence that the distillation is not overclaiming, and they are rendered: 13 source units produced no rule for resume-design, 7 for job-search, 29 for system-design, 30 for app-architecture, each with its own reason and creator profile — e.g. 'raptor:theme:5 Modular Monoliths Beat the Microservices Mess · 76 chunks · 4 videos · 3 creators — 87% of the theme's chunks are NDC Conferences' and 'raptor:theme:24 Coupling is not bad; balance strength, volatility, distance · 33 chunks · 1 videos · 1 creators — only one of this pack's videos is in the theme'. A pack that logs 30 places it looked and found nothing usable is making a smaller and more believable claim than one that does not.

Contested rubrics are 0 in all four packs, and the checks strip says so rather than hiding it. The panel therefore advertises a 'contested' badge that nothing currently earns — consistent with V7 being recorded as short of genuine cross-creator disagreements, and worth reading as a corpus limitation rather than a rendering one.

Screenshots are 1008x761 crops of an 1152x870 window rather than the harness's 1440x900; the pack card lays out at 1106px, so the pin column sits inside the window but outside the capture. Shot 06 was taken at 0.78 page zoom for that reason. No check in this verdict makes a layout or clipping claim.

Other agents were driving the same browser profile and the same server throughout: tabs were created, navigated and closed under this evaluation, and the corpus was being ingested into. The tab used for the readings recorded here was created for this evaluation and its readings were re-verified against the pack files after the fact; where a reading could have been contaminated by a concurrent action it was retaken.

RE-CHECK 2026-08-11: check 27, the only one this verdict failed, was re-run after its fix was built. REDUCED INDEPENDENCE, stated plainly: the same agent built the notice and re-checked it, because the Claude spend limit was terminating subagents — so for this one check the project's builder-is-not-evaluator rule did not hold. The other 36 checks are untouched and remain the independent evaluator's work, including the 105-of-105 citation resolution it verified by reading each cited chunk rather than trusting quote_resolution.

Related fix verified in the same pass, from V8's evaluator (task #69): the ablation 'decisive' badge used to fire by fallback on every metric except criteria_recall, because runner_max read a *_max spread key that only criteria_recall has — so evidence_precision and provenance always rendered 'leader clears the runner-up's own spread', a comparison never performed. winner() now returns a three-way basis and the panel reads 'EVIDENCE_PRECISION merged | scored once - reliability unmeasured'. Verdicts are recomputed at read time in both the pack reader and the build-report reader, so runs committed before the fix get the corrected reading rather than serving the old one forever. Recomputing also revealed criteria_recall is TIED between raptor and merged at 0.2632, which the stored verdict had shown as a merged lead.
